s1.syndrome_frame: Progressively enlarging, painless, ulcerated skin lesions with central crusting in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Painless nodular lesions on the forehead and right cheek
Arborizing telangiectasias and peripheral pigment on dermoscopy
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Lesions were initially observed as erythematous nodules 3 months prior
Lesions gradually increased in size
No fever, pain, or discharge from the lesions
Patient has a history of kidney transplant in 2004
Patient is immunocompromised
Lesions are firm with central ulceration and hemorrhagic crusting
Dermoscopy showed arborizing telangiectasias, central ulceration with crusting, and peripheral pigment
Histopathological examination showed extensive dermal collection of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and macrophages
Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified on histopathological examination

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified on histopathological examination, consistent with Cryptococcosis, particularly in an immunocompromised patient

shortlist.label: Blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressively enlarging, painless, ulcerated skin lesions with central crusting are consistent with Blastomycosis, and the patient's immunocompromised status increases the risk

shortlist.label: Histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and histopathological findings could be consistent with Histoplasmosis, especially given the patient's immunocompromised status and the presence of intracellular organisms

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: The lesions' appearance, including central ulceration and crusting, could be consistent with Basal cell carcinoma, although the patient's immunocompromised status and the presence of intracellular yeasts make infectious causes more likely

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's age and the appearance of the lesions, including central ulceration and crusting, could be consistent with Squamous cell carcinoma, although the presence of intracellular yeasts and the patient's immunocompromised status make infectious causes more plausible

raw.rationale: The presence of intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos on histopathological examination is a key feature of Cryptococcosis, especially in an immunocompromised patient.

rejected.label: Blastomycosis
rejected.why: While Blastomycosis can present with similar skin lesions, the histopathological findings do not specifically support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Histoplasmosis
rejected.why: Histoplasmosis typically presents with systemic symptoms and the histopathological findings do not match those described in the case.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The presence of intracellular yeasts and the patient's immunocompromised status make a fungal infection more likely than a skin cancer like basal cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathological findings do not support a diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma, which typically shows malignant squamous cells on histopathology.
